# Shared wire fixtures

Portable JSON scenarios for client implementers of Apron protocol v6. Expected
state is written from `PROTOCOL.md`, not generated by the example client or
backend. `references` holds repository-relative specification links. These
scenarios exercise selected protocol behaviors; passing them is not full
client conformance.

## Run

From the repository root, after `make install`:

```sh
make test-web   # replay fixtures and frontend unit tests
make test-wire  # session fixtures over real loopback WebSockets
make test       # both suites and Go tests; also runs in CI
```

Replay uses the frontend's existing Vitest setup. Session tests use the actual
TypeScript client with Node.js 24 WebSockets and a small Go transport peer;
no browser or running example server is needed. No new dependencies are required.

## Common structure

Each file has `format: 4`, `kind` (`replay` or `session`), `name`,
`description`, `references`, `variants`, and `expected`, and no other
top-level keys. Frames are protocol 6. Each variant has `name` and ordered
`steps`, starts with fresh client state, and must reach the top-level
`expected` state. An `expect` step additionally checks an intermediate state.

Each step is an object with exactly one key, the operation. Objects are
unordered; arrays are ordered. All IDs are JSON strings. Small IDs such as
`"100"` are readable epoch-millisecond values near the Unix epoch; they are
positive and below `2^53`, and every comparison of `log_id`s or
`message_id`s is numeric (`"9" < "10"`).

Run every variant twice: once with the literal frames, once with
`"jsonrpc": "2.0"` added at the top level of each incoming frame (including
replies built from `reply` steps). Do not alter nested data. Outgoing client
frames may use either envelope. Expectations never depend on a generated
request ID or on optional envelope fields.

## Records, replay, and the logical projection

Both suites share one client-side model (PROTOCOL.md [§2](../../../PROTOCOL.md#2-identifiers), [§3.4](../../../PROTOCOL.md#34-rooms), [§3.5](../../../PROTOCOL.md#35-messages),
[§4.1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#41-history)–[§4.5](../../../PROTOCOL.md#45-reactions)). The client keeps four stores, one record per key:

| record | key | sources |
|---|---|---|
| room record | `room_id` | `room_list` results (`joined` and `not_joined`), `room_update` notifications (`joined` and `updated`), history `rooms` |
| message snapshot | `message_id` | `message` notifications with a `message_id`, history `messages`, embedded snapshots |
| reaction set | `(message_id, user_id)` | `reactions` notifications, history `reactions` (one set per element of `reactions[]`) |
| membership | `(room_id, user.user_id)` | `membership` notifications, history `membership` (one per element of `members[]`) |

**Replay rule.** A record replaces the stored record for its key only when its
`log_id` is numerically greater; an equal or lower `log_id` is ignored. This
holds regardless of source (live, history, embedded) and arrival order. A
reaction or membership element takes its record's `log_id`. The only
exception: a room record without `log_id` (a server without cap `history`,
which may omit it) always replaces. Replacement is whole: omitted fields
disappear, objects and arrays are never merged, and `null` is a stored value.

**Member lists.** A room's `members` in a `room_list` result or a
`room_update` `joined` is complete ([PROTOCOL.md §4.3.1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#431-listing)): it replaces the
room's member list as of the same room's `latest_log_id` in that frame (the
list's position). Memberships at or below the position are already in it and
are ignored; greater ones apply on top by the replay rule, whether they arrived
before the list or after. A frame without `latest_log_id` gives a list without
a position, which memberships always override. A room's members are the users
whose latest membership has `joined: true`; each is the object the list or the
winning membership gave.

**Decoding.**

- Message notifications are flat snapshots:
  `{"method":"message","params":{message_id, log_id, room_id, from, body?, reply_to?, deleted?, ext?}}`.
  History `messages` are the same flat objects. Other keys, such as
  `prev_log_id` and `prev_room_id`, are ignored. A `message` notification
  without `message_id` (such as a `@private` notice) is a **transient
  notice**: it is shown for the session, never installed, and never replaces
  or reorders anything ([PROTOCOL.md §3.5](../../../PROTOCOL.md#35-messages), [Appendix A.1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#a1-system-identities-and-scoped-notices)).
- A history result is `{rooms?, messages?, reactions?, membership?, first_log_id?, last_log_id?, more, latest_log_id, history_log_id}`.
  A missing array is empty. Install every record in all four arrays. Do not filter records by the
  requested room: a move snapshot in room A's history carries `room_id` B and
  must re-home the message into B.
- `reply_to` (on messages) and `intro_message` (on room records) are message
  objects. An object with a `log_id` is an **embedded snapshot**: install it
  in the message store by the replay rule, in its own `room_id`. An object
  without `log_id` is a **bare reference** (`{message_id}`) and installs
  nothing.
- A room record is an element of a `room_list` result's `joined` or
  `not_joined`, of a `room_update`'s `joined` or `updated`, or of a history
  result's `rooms`. Its delivery fields (`latest_log_id`, `history_log_id`,
  `members`) are not part of the record; `members` starts the room's member
  list (above). A `left` array, in a `room_update` or a `room_list` result,
  holds no records: it only removes rooms from the visible set (sessions
  only).
- A membership is `{"method":"membership","params":{log_id, room_id, members: [{user, joined}]}}`;
  history `membership` elements have the same shape. `user` is a recorded
  user object, stored and projected as given.
- Unknown top-level keys (in frames, records, results, and reaction elements)
  must be ignored and may be dropped. They never break replay. Keys such as
  `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `"hasOwnProperty"`, and `"toString"` appear
  as unknown keys, inside `ext`, and as room and user IDs; they must not
  pollute prototypes or collide with built-in properties.

**Message projection.** The stored snapshot restricted to the known fields
`message_id`, `log_id`, `room_id`, `from`, `body`, `reply_to`, `deleted`, and
`ext`, each present exactly when present in the snapshot and copied exactly
(`from`, `body`, and `ext` are compared deeply, including `null`s, unknown
embed kinds, and `"__proto__"` keys inside `ext`). `reply_to` is always
projected bare, as `{"message_id": ...}`. No defaults are materialized
(`body.format` stays absent when absent). Then:

- `reactions`: present only when the message is not a tombstone
  (`deleted !== true`) and at least one stored set for the message is
  non-empty. It is an array of `{"emoji": string, "user_ids": [string]}`,
  one per distinct emoji across all users' sets, sorted by emoji in Unicode
  code point order; `user_ids` are sorted by string order. Duplicate emoji in
  a set collapse. Reaction sets for messages that are not loaded are kept and
  appear once the message arrives. A tombstone hides reactions; its stored sets
  are kept but not projected.

**Room projection.** `{room_id, log_id?, parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message?, ext?, members?, messages}`:
the optional record fields come from the stored room record (absent when the
record lacks them or no record is stored), `intro_message` is projected bare as
`{"message_id": ...}`, and `messages` lists the message projections whose
current `room_id` is this room, in numeric `message_id` order. In replay,
`members` is present when anything is known about the room's members: its
members' user objects, sorted by `user_id` (sessions project members
separately, see Session state). The room projection never includes delivery
fields or defaults (no `title` fallback).

Internal maps, caches, DOM elements, recovery buffers, and checkpoints are not
assertions. Compare projections exactly after the normalization above.

## Replay scenarios

A replay fixture accepts `receive` and `expect` steps and has no room of its
own; the store spans all rooms and includes every room with a stored record, a
message homed in it, or member state.

```json
{
  "format": 4,
  "kind": "replay",
  "name": "Creation snapshot",
  "description": "...",
  "references": ["PROTOCOL.md#35-messages"],
  "variants": [{
    "name": "live",
    "steps": [{"receive": {"method": "message", "params": {
      "message_id": "100", "log_id": "100", "room_id": "general",
      "from": {"user_id": "alice"}, "body": {"text": "original"}
    }}}]
  }],
  "expected": {"rooms": [{"room_id": "general", "messages": [
    {"message_id": "100", "log_id": "100", "room_id": "general",
     "from": {"user_id": "alice"}, "body": {"text": "original"}}
  ]}]}
}
```

`receive` holds a `message`, `room_update`, `reactions`, or `membership`
notification, or a response `{id, result}` to `history` (it has `more`) or to
`room_list` (it has `joined` or `not_joined`). Fixed response IDs label
already-issued requests; this suite tests reduction, not request scheduling.
History metadata (`first_log_id`, `last_log_id`, `more`, `latest_log_id`,
`history_log_id`) describes the source log slice before compaction and is not
interpreted by replay.

`expected` and `expect` are `{"rooms": [...]}`: every room that has a stored
record, at least one message currently homed in it, or member state, sorted by
`room_id` in string order, each in the room projection above.

| file | covers |
|---|---|
| `01-creation.json` | flat creation snapshot, live and from history |
| `02-full-replacement.json` | omitted `body.format`, `reply_to`, and `ext` namespaces are removed; `ext` replaced, not merged |
| `03-literal-null.json` | `null` stored inside `ext` and embeds |
| `04-array-replacement.json` | embeds arrays replaced whole |
| `05-tombstone.json` | tombstone wins over stale content; tombstones hide reactions (raw and compacted history) |
| `06-duplicate-replay.json` | repeated room records, snapshots, and reaction sets are ignored |
| `07-snapshot-loaded.json` | history snapshot replaces a loaded message |
| `08-snapshot-unloaded.json` | an edit installs without its creation |
| `09-history-equivalence.json` | live, raw page, two pages delivered newest-first, and compacted page converge across all record kinds |
| `10-ext-and-unknown-keys.json` | `ext` survives exactly; unknown and prototype-like keys, room IDs, and user IDs are safe |
| `11-numeric-ordering.json` | numeric `log_id` comparison for every kind; numeric `message_id` order |
| `12-room-moves.json` | move into a thread room re-homes rather than deletes; move snapshot in both rooms' history; stale source pages cannot pull it back; reactions follow |
| `13-room-records.json` | room records from `room_list`, `room_update`, and history replace in full; embedded `intro_message`; stale room record; thread room with `parent_room_id`; an omitted empty history array |
| `14-reactions.json` | per-user sets, duplicate collapse, `[]` clears, reactions before their message, folded compacted records |
| `15-embedded-snapshots.json` | `reply_to` and `intro_message` snapshots install by the replay rule; stale embeds ignored; bare and dangling references install nothing |
| `16-transient-notices.json` | `message` notifications without `message_id` install nothing, with or without `room_id`; a logged `@server` notice is an ordinary snapshot in the room it names |
| `17-memberships.json` | memberships by the replay rule from live, raw and compacted history; a complete `members` list as of its room's head, before or after newer memberships; leaves kept through compaction |

The TypeScript adapter is
[`clients/web/src/lib/protocol/wire-replay.test.ts`](../../../clients/web/src/lib/protocol/wire-replay.test.ts).
Another client needs only a JSON loader, a frame-to-store adapter, and the
projection above.

## Session scenarios

Session fixtures use `kind: "session"`. They drive the real client over a
transport: the fixture plays the server, and operation steps call the
client's public API.

### Steps

| step | meaning |
|---|---|
| `receive: frame` | Deliver the literal server frame. |
| `request: {as, match}` | Take the next matching outgoing client request (see below), assert it, and capture its runtime `id` under `as`. |
| `reply: {to, result}` / `reply: {to, error}` | Send `{id, result}` or `{id, error}` for the request captured as `to`. |
| `send: {as, room?, text, format, reply_to?, mentions?}` | Post a message to `room`, or without `room` to the server's default room; `reply_to` is a message ID, `mentions` a list of `user_id`s. |
| `command: {as, room?, text, mentions?}` | Send `text` as a `command` (cap `command`) in `room`, or without `room` in the default room. |
| `editMessage: {as, message_id, text}` | Save the message with only `body.text` changed. |
| `moveMessage: {as, message_id, room}` | Save the message with `room_id` changed to `room`. |
| `deleteMessage: {as, message_id}` | Save the message as a tombstone. |
| `react: {as, message_id, emojis}` | Set the user's complete emoji set on the message (`[]` clears). |
| `createRoom: {as, parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message_id?}` | Create a room; with `parent_room_id` it is a thread. |
| `updateRoom: {as, room, title?, intro_message_id?}` | Patch a room's metadata: a present key sets the value (`null` clears it), an absent key keeps the current value. |
| `joinRoom: {as, room}` / `leaveRoom: {as, room}` | Join or leave a room (or thread). |
| `listRooms: {as, parent_room_id?}` | List the rooms not joined (with their members), or with `parent_room_id` that room's threads not joined. |
| `loadRoom: {as, room}` | Open a thread room (a room with `parent_room_id`): load its history as its own room. |
| `loadOlder: {as, room}` | Load the page of a thread room's history just before what `loadRoom` loaded. |
| `disconnect: true` | Close the transport; subsequent frames go to a fresh connection. |
| `expect: state` | Wait for the given keys of the session state (bounded deadline). |

Each operation step (`send` through `loadOlder`) tracks its outcome under its
`as` label in `operations`: `pending` when invoked, then `fulfilled` or
`rejected`. Mutations settle on the reply to their request: a `result`
fulfills, an `error` rejects. They never wait for a broadcast. Servers send
the notifications a request causes on the requesting connection before its
result ([PROTOCOL.md §1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#1-transport--framing)), and the fixtures do, but a conforming client does not
depend on it (a broadcast may also not come at all). `loadRoom` and
`loadOlder` fulfill when their page is applied and reject on an error or
invalid page. Operation and capture labels are unique within a variant.

### Request matching

A `request` step selects the oldest queued client request whose `method`
equals `match.method` and whose `params.room_id` and `params.message_id` each
equal the value in `match.params`, where absent equals absent. Unrelated
requests (for example `me` or `activity`) may be pipelined or reordered and
stay queued. Then:

- `match` is a recursive subset of the frame: objects match by listed keys;
  arrays and scalars match exactly. Extra fields such as `auth.params.name`,
  `auth.params.client`, and `history.params.limit` are unconstrained.
- For mutations (`message`, `command`, `room_set`, `room_join`,
  `room_leave`, `reactions`) `params` must equal `match.params` exactly, to
  catch lost or unwanted fields.
- Captured IDs must be strings, distinct from every earlier captured ID in the
  variant.

### What a conforming client sends

These are exact (PROTOCOL.md [§3.5](../../../PROTOCOL.md#35-messages), [§4.2](../../../PROTOCOL.md#42-edit), [§4.3](../../../PROTOCOL.md#43-rooms), [§4.5](../../../PROTOCOL.md#45-reactions), [§4.8](../../../PROTOCOL.md#48-command)). "Latest snapshot" and
"latest record" mean the stored record under the replay rule at the moment the
operation is invoked.

| operation | method | `params` |
|---|---|---|
| `send` | `message` | `{room_id?: room, body: {text, format, mentions?}, reply_to?: {message_id}}`: no `room_id` without `room`; `mentions` only when given |
| `command` | `command` | `{room_id?: room, body: {text, mentions?}}`: `text` as typed, slash included |
| `editMessage` | `message` | latest snapshot's client fields with `body.text` replaced: `{message_id, room_id, body, reply_to?, ext?}`; `body` keeps `format`, `embeds`, and any other body keys |
| `moveMessage` | `message` | `{message_id, room_id: room, body, reply_to?, ext?}` from the latest snapshot |
| `deleteMessage` | `message` | `{message_id, room_id, reply_to?, ext?, deleted: true}` from the latest snapshot; no `body` |
| `react` | `reactions` | `{message_id, emojis}` with `emojis` as given |
| `createRoom` | `room_set` | `{parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message?: {message_id}}`: only the keys given; no `room_id`, no `ext` |
| `updateRoom` | `room_set` | `{room_id, title?, intro_message?: {message_id}, ext?}` from the latest record with the patch applied; never `parent_room_id` |
| `joinRoom` / `leaveRoom` | `room_join` / `room_leave` | `{room_id: room}` |
| `listRooms` | `room_list` | `{filter: "not_joined", members: true}`, or `{parent_room_id, filter: "not_joined"}` |
| (recovery) | `history` | `{room_id, after, before}`, or `{room_id, after}` for a resume sent behind `auth` (see below), plus an optional positive `limit` |
| (connect) | `auth` | `{scheme: "guest"}`, or `{scheme: "token", token}` when an earlier `auth` result on the session carried a `token` and the server offers `token`, plus optional `name`/`client` |
| (right behind `auth`, cap `rooms`) | `room_list` | `{filter: "joined", members: true}`, plus `latest_log_id` on a token resume (see below); sent before the `auth` result |

In saves, `reply_to` is always resubmitted bare even when the stored snapshot
embedded it, `ext` is resubmitted unchanged (including `"__proto__"` keys),
`deleted` is omitted unless deleting, and fields absent from the latest
snapshot stay absent. Room updates resubmit `intro_message` bare and `ext`
unchanged.

### Connecting

`auth` is a barrier ([PROTOCOL.md §3.2](../../../PROTOCOL.md#32-authentication)): on each `server` frame that starts a
connection the client sends `auth`, the joined listing, and the resumes below
back to back, without waiting for the `auth` result. If `auth` fails, the
requests behind it are denied and change nothing.

- **Joined listing.** Its `joined` becomes the visible set. A result with
  `left` lists changes since `latest_log_id`: rooms in `joined` are shown or
  refreshed, rooms in `left` go, and every other room kept from the lost
  connection stays as it was. A result without `left` is a full listing: kept
  rooms missing from its `joined` go.
- **Listing changes since a position.** Only on a token resume, when the
  previous connection's joined listing arrived: `latest_log_id` is the least,
  over the joined rooms kept from it, of each room's checkpoint C (a room that
  recovers automatically; a room whose last recovery failed has none) or its
  known head (a thread). If any kept room has neither, or none is kept, the
  listing is a full one. A result for another identity than the kept rooms'
  (the `auth` result names someone else) is not applied: the client lists
  again in full.
- **Resumes.** Each joined top-level room kept from the lost connection with a
  checkpoint C resumes its recovery at once, before any room record names its
  head: it requests `{room_id, after: max(C + 1, F)}` without `before`, takes H
  from the first page's `latest_log_id`, and continues as below. Its live
  records are buffered from then on. The listing then decides whether the room
  stays; one that goes stops recovering.

### History recovery profile

The fixtures pin the example client's recovery profile. It is a test profile
built from [PROTOCOL.md §4.1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#41-history), not
the only conforming strategy. The recovery state below is kept per room across
a lost connection (see Session state); a room that becomes visible for the
first time starts without it. A **room record frame** below is any frame that
carries a visible room's record: the `room_list` result that lists it as
joined, or a `room_update` that lists it in `joined` or `updated`.

- **Head and bound.** Per visible room the client tracks its known head, the
  greatest `latest_log_id` from that room's record frames and history results
  and `log_id` of live records (memberships included) delivered with that
  `room_id`, and its floor F,
  the greatest effective lower bound seen: `history_log_id`, or the same
  frame's or page's own `latest_log_id + 1` when it is `null`. Before any
  bound is seen there is no F.
- **Eviction.** When F grows, the client drops the room's messages whose stored
  snapshot `log_id` is below F, drops buffered and newly received message and
  reaction records below F, and ignores page records below F. Room records are
  not evicted.
- **Automatic recovery** (cap `history`, rooms without `parent_room_id`, no
  recovery already running), with H = the known head:
  - A room record frame starts one when the room becomes visible with no kept state,
    when its last recovery failed, when there is no checkpoint C yet, or when
    the known head is above C. It is a **rebuild** (clear the room's messages
    and their reaction sets, start at `after = F`) for a room with no kept
    state, after a failure, or with no C; otherwise it **resumes** at
    `after = max(C + 1, F)` and keeps the room's state. A room kept from a
    lost connection whose head has not moved past C needs no request. A room
    shown without a record (no cap `rooms`) takes its head from the first
    message delivered for it on each connection.
  - When F grows outside a recovery and there is no C or `C + 1 < F`, a rebuild
    starts.
  - If `after > H` the recovery completes with no request.
- **Pages.** Request `{room_id, after, before: H}`, apply each valid page's
  records, and continue from `last_log_id + 1` (numerically) while `more`. H
  never changes during a recovery once known, even when frames or pages report
  a newer head. Memberships in pages apply to the room's member list whatever
  the floor.
- **Live records during recovery** for that room are buffered and applied when
  the recovery completes or fails. A room record frame during a recovery never
  starts another one.
- **Overtaken.** If a page's bound, or F after a room record frame, is greater than
  the pending `after`, history was discarded: ignore that page and any pending
  request, rebuild from the new F with the same H, and keep buffered records at
  or above F. A bound equal to `after` only evicts.
- **Completion.** Apply the buffer; C becomes `max(C, H)`.
- **Failure.** An `error` reply; a result lacking a boolean `more`, a valid
  `latest_log_id`, or a `history_log_id` that is null or a valid ID, or with a
  record key (`rooms`, `messages`, `reactions`, `membership`) that is present
  but not an array; or a `more: true` page whose `last_log_id` is below
  `after` or not below H. The client applies the pages it has and the buffer, leaves C
  unchanged, and marks the room failed; the next room record frame for it rebuilds.
  A failure is not retried on a timer (the `retry_after` variant's
  `data.retry_after` is not waited on).
- **Thread rooms** never recover automatically. `loadRoom` loads one with
  H = its known head when invoked. Without a checkpoint it requests only the
  newest page, `{room_id, before: H}` with no `after`; T becomes H, and the
  page's `first_log_id` (with `more: true`) marks where older records remain.
  `loadOlder` then requests `{room_id, before: first_log_id - 1}`, one page at a
  time, until a page has `more: false` or F passes that position. With a
  checkpoint T, kept across a lost connection, `loadRoom` pages forward from
  `max(T + 1, F)` to H: pages apply as they arrive; if F overtakes `after`,
  continue from F; T advances to each page's `last_log_id` and to H at
  `more: false`. Live records for the thread apply directly. (A thread the
  user has not joined delivers nothing live; the example client can open one
  without joining it and load it the same way, but the fixtures do not.)

The fixtures assert no state while a recovery has requests in flight; they
assert after completion, after failure, or before recovery starts.

### Session state

The normalized session state has these keys:

- `you`: the identity from the latest successful `auth` result on the current
  connection, or `null`.
- `caps`: the latest `server` frame's `caps` sorted by string order; `[]` when
  omitted or before any `server` frame on the connection.
- `rooms`: the visible rooms sorted by `room_id` in string order, each in the
  room projection above without `members`. With cap `rooms` they are the rooms
  joined on the current connection: the joined listing sent behind `auth`
  (above), plus `room_update` `joined`, minus `left`. Without it they are the
  rooms a `message` arrived in on the current connection. A `room_id` starting
  with `@` is an ordinary room. A client's placeholder for the default room
  before its `room_id` is known is not a room. Only server records appear;
  optimistic local echoes do not.
- `users`: the kept user objects, one per `user_id`, keyed by `user_id` in
  string order, merged field by field ([PROTOCOL.md §3.3](../../../PROTOCOL.md#33-identity)) from current objects only:
  `you`, `new` in `user` notifications, and room `members` and `users` in
  `room_list` results and `room_update` notifications. Recorded objects (a
  message's or reaction's `from`, a membership's `user`) and `activity`
  senders never merge. `old` with `new` makes the old `user_id` stand for the
  new one; it merges nothing.
- `members`: for each visible room whose member list is known, keyed by
  `room_id`, the `user_id`s of its members (Member lists, above) in string
  order.
- `senders`: for each message in a visible room, keyed by `message_id`, its
  sender as rendered: field by field, the kept object for the `from`'s
  `user_id` (or the identity that replaced it), else the `from` itself.
- `notices`: the transient notices received this session, in arrival order,
  each `{room_id, from, body?}` (`room_id` as sent).
- `directory`: the `room_id`s of the latest `listRooms` result without
  `parent_room_id`, in the order listed.
- `typing`: active typing indicators `{room_id, from}` ([PROTOCOL.md §4.4](../../../PROTOCOL.md#44-activity)),
  sorted by `room_id` then `from.user_id`. An `activity` frame with
  `typing > 0` adds or refreshes one; `typing: 0` removes it; an `activity`
  frame without `typing` leaves it unchanged. Fixture servers that send
  `activity` advertise cap `activity`.
- `operations`: operation labels mapped to `pending`, `fulfilled`, or
  `rejected`.

On `disconnect` the client's protocol view is rebuilt from the next
connection: `you` is `null`, `caps` and `typing` are `[]`, and `rooms` is `[]`
until rooms are listed again. The record stores (member lists included),
floors, checkpoints, users, and notices are kept, so each room listed again
resumes from its checkpoint rather than recovering in full ([PROTOCOL.md §4.1](../../../PROTOCOL.md#41-history), recovery from `C + 1`). (The UI may keep showing the old view meanwhile; that is not part
of the projection.) A pending operation across a disconnect is unconstrained.

An omitted top-level `expected` key is unconstrained; `expected: {}` means
each variant ends with its own `expect`. Supplied values compare exactly.
Adapters wait for state changes with bounded deadlines; fixture files contain
no sleeps, timers, or DOM selectors.

| file | covers |
|---|---|
| `auth-barrier.json` | `auth` and the joined listing sent back to back; after a failed `auth` the denied listing changes nothing |
| `core-session.json` | a server without cap `rooms`: guest auth, a first post without `room_id` whose broadcast names the default room before the result, `activity` typing, bare `reply_to` answered by an embedded snapshot, a `@private` notice, `server` replacement, unknown notifications, rooms learned from their messages including one whose ID starts with `@`, and a logged `@server` notice in the room it names |
| `commands.json` | `command` with and without mentions, its result and error, a `@private` reply that is never stored, and `body.mentions` on a message |
| `membership.json` | the joined set with members from the listing behind `auth`, the guest's own join before the `auth` result, `listRooms` with members, `joinRoom` and `leaveRoom` settling on `{}` after their memberships and `room_update` `joined` and `left`, others' memberships keeping member lists current, an `updated` thread not joined staying hidden, removal by the server |
| `room-list-delta.json` | a token resume lists only the joined rooms changed since the kept checkpoints and resumes the kept rooms behind `auth`; `left` removes rooms and keeps the others, a result without `left` is a full listing |
| `message-saves.json` | edit, move into a thread room, and delete resubmit `room_id`, `body`, bare `reply_to`, and `ext` from the latest snapshot |
| `rooms.json` | thread and top-level creation with `room_set`, patch-style updates resubmitting `title`, `intro_message`, and `ext`, full record replacement, `left` |
| `users.json` | field-by-field merges of current objects from `you`, `members`, `users`, and `user`; `from` and membership users never merge; senders render from the kept object, else their `from`; memberships change member lists, not users |
| `reactions.json` | react, change, clear, move re-log in the destination, `invalid_params`, tombstone hiding |
| `request-errors.json` | denied send, save, and room creation keep the session usable |
| `history-live-boundary.json` | fixed H with live records above it (edit, room update, reaction), mixed-kind pages (limit counts every kind), raw and compacted |
| `history-boundaries.json` | inclusive bound with eviction, bound overtaking a recovery by `room_update` or by page, sparse IDs, `null` bounds (empty log, expired cache, becoming retained, page head) |
| `history-recovery-failure.json` | a head above the checkpoint resumes from `C + 1`; an error or invalid page keeps partial and buffered state; the next room record frame rebuilds |
| `reconnect-history.json` | new guest identity after reconnect with a full listing; the kept room's recovery resumes from its checkpoint behind `auth`, without a head, across message and reaction records |
| `thread-recovery.json` | thread room loaded only by `loadRoom`, newest page first and an older page by `loadOlder`, as its own room; move in both rooms' logs; interleaved with room recovery |

The Node adapter is [`tests/interop/wire.spec.ts`](../../interop/wire.spec.ts).
Its [`wire-peer.go`](../../interop/wire-peer.go) utility only transports frames;
it contains no chat behavior or expected state. Each test gets a fresh client
connection. Alternative implementations can use any transport harness that
preserves these exchanges and projections.

## Fixture invariants

Every session variant describes one plausible server, and these hold (they
were checked with an independent reference reducer and client):

- Each `log_id` names one record (one key, one content) across the whole
  variant, across connections, and in embedded copies. `log_id`s are one
  server-wide sequence: new live records on a connection arrive in strictly
  increasing order, and above every `latest_log_id` already reported for their
  room. A message's earliest snapshot is its creation, with
  `log_id == message_id`.
- A room record frame's `latest_log_id` is at least every record already delivered
  for the room; a page's is at least the room's head known when it was
  requested and at least its `last_log_id` (it may be captured before later live
  frames). A non-null `history_log_id` never exceeds `latest_log_id`, and the
  effective bound never decreases. Records may be missing from live delivery
  (a server may drop notifications); a later head reveals them.
- A room's log holds its room records, its reaction records, its memberships
  (unless the server keeps a guest's out of the log, as a server MAY), and
  every snapshot of a message that was in the room just before or after it, so
  a move appears in both rooms.
- History pages hold only records of the requested room within
  `[after, before]`, ascending per array, and no `users`; empty arrays may be
  omitted. `first_log_id`/`last_log_id` span the slice before compaction;
  records missing inside it were compacted into later records of the same key
  in the page. The slice starts at the first record at
  or after `after`, and `more` is true exactly when records remain up to
  `before`. The server clamps `limit` per file (stated in each description)
  and counts records of every kind.
- Mutation results name the saved message, the created message's creation
  snapshot, or the created or updated room (`room_set`); `reactions`,
  `room_join`, `room_leave`, and successful `command` results are `{}`. They
  follow the notifications their request caused on the connection.
- A `room_list` with `members: true` carries each room's complete `members`
  and a `users` array; a `room_update` `joined` carries `members`. A joined
  listing with `latest_log_id` either has `left` (possibly empty) or is a full
  listing.
- A `room_update` `updated` for a room not joined describes a new or edited
  thread in a joined room; `left` names only rooms that were visible.

Replay variants obey the same one-record-per-`log_id` rule and the history
metadata constraints that do not depend on request bounds.

## Scope and additions

Keep fixture expectations explicit and reviewable. Add variants only when
they must produce the same final state (or use `expected: {}` with a final
`expect` per variant); use intermediate `expect` steps when ordering matters.
Keep the invariants above when adding frames. Use generated data for volume
benchmarks rather than large checked-in logs.

Not covered: `me` response semantics, liveness `ping` and `away` (they depend
on timers and focus; the client's unit tests cover them), opening a thread
without joining it, typing expiry, read markers, deduplication lifetime,
embeds and uploads (including `/avatar`), push, RTC, WebAuthn (see
`tests/fixtures/webauthn.json`), renderer behavior beyond `senders`, and
performance.
